title: unify-terraform-private-state-layout-gpu-iam-networking-migration
author: Avery Chen
release_notes: Unify Terraform state layout for Private deployments: migrate GPU node pools, IAM roles, and networking into a single, consistent remote-state layout. Includes migration scripts, docs, and rollout plan. No runtime behavior changes expected; follow upgrade steps in README to migrate state with minimal downtime.
body: Motivation: Private deployments currently have several duplicated terraform state layouts for GPU node pools, IAM, and networking across regions and installer flavors (helm vs on-prem). This fragmentation makes upgrades, rollbacks, and multi-region imports error-prone and slows automation work (ENG-4821). This PR unifies the remote state layout and reorganizes modules so that private deployments use a consistent state namespace and module boundaries. Changes included: 1) new top-level module private/state that references child modules for compute (gpu_node_pools), iam, and networking; 2) migration script terraform/scripts/migrate-state.sh that uses temporary workspaces and git-backed state locking to move resources into the new state layout; 3) backward-compatible wrapper modules so existing overlays continue to work during rollout; 4) updates to installer docs and CI to validate both pre- and post-migration plans. Migration plan (high level): - run `terraform init` in the migration harness and validate plan against a dry-run GCP project - run `terraform state mv` operations recorded by the script under maintenance window - assert drift-free after migration using `terraform plan` and integration tests - can rollback by switching overlay to the compatibility wrapper branch and moving state back using the same script. Testing: - unit-level terraform validate and fmt checks (CI) - integration canary in staging: deployed 3 private clusters across eu-west1/us-central1 and verified node autoscaling, GPU scheduling, and private network peering - IAM bindings verified with small service account access checks (no changes to permissions) Author notes: kept module interfaces stable where possible, added deprecation comments for the old layouts. See linear/ENG-4821 for rollout checklist and OPS-197 for runbook. This PR intentionally does not change runtime behavior; focuses on state layout and DX for operators.
commits_summary: Init: split out private/state module and glue modules for gpu_node_pools, iam, networking
Add: migration script terraform/scripts/migrate-state.sh and README with step-by-step rollback/verify
Refactor: compatibility wrapper modules for existing overlays and integration tests
CI: add matrix job to validate pre- and post-migration plans and state moves
Docs: update private-installer/README.md and upgrade runbook
review_comments: Ravi Singh: Left a few nit comments around state locking and GCS bucket naming; requested explicit bucket lifecycle policy to avoid accidental deletion during migration.
Avery Chen: Addressed Rafi's notes and added `gcs_bucket_retention` variable with sensible default; clarified lock TTL in the migration script.
Elena Morales: Asked for stronger test coverage around node pool taints and GPU quota checks during migration. Requested that we add a canary step to CI.
Avery Chen: Added canary job in ci/terraform-migration-matrix.yml and integration test that validates GPU scheduling in staging clusters.
Samir Patel: Verified IAM bindings and approved after confirming there was no privilege escalation risk.
CI: All checks passed after fixes; final approval granted by Elena and Samir.
notes_for_ops: Run terraform/scripts/migrate-state.sh from a bastion host with gsutil access and Terraform v1.6+. Ensure state bucket retention is set and locks are respected. Follow linear/ENG-4821 for the step-by-step maintenance window script. Rollback instructions are in terraform/scripts/migrate-state.sh -- use the compatibility wrapper branch if rollback is needed.
upgrade_rollback_plan: Upgrade: run migration script in staging and then in prod maintenance windows, validate post-migration plans and run integration sanity checks. Rollback: apply compatibility wrapper overlay and use migration script to move state back; verify plans are drift-free. Full steps in private-installer/README.md
testing_summary: Staging canary across eu-west1/us-central1 validated node autoscaling and GPU scheduling. Integration tests assert no IAM regressions. CI validates pre/post plans and state move commands. No failures observed in canary runs.
changelog_excerpt: Unify Private terraform state layout for gpu node pools, IAM, and networking; add migration tooling and documentation. Operators should follow the included runbook when upgrading.

OPS-197: schedule production migration window and runbook rehearsal
